discovery: Discovery of geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University, Israel and Chapman University, USA

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed in 1959 that electromagnetic potentials, not just fields, have physical consequences: charged particles acquire a measurable phase when encircling a flux they never touch. Berry's 1984 discovery generalised this to the geometric phase acquired by any quantum system transported adiabatically around a closed loop in parameter space. These ideas transformed how physicists think about quantum states, revealing that geometry and topology are built into quantum theory. They now underpin our understanding of the quantum Hall effect, topological insulators, polarization in solids, anomalous velocities, and geometric quantum gates, and are confirmed in electron holography, optics, and cold-atom experiments. Both started from questions many considered unphysical, and both reshaped the conceptual and experimental landscape of modern physics. Aharonov's later work on weak values further opened new routes to probing quantum foundations in the laboratory.
